programmes.name_local: 發展品牌、升級轉型及拓展內銷市場的專項基金（BUD專項基金）
programmes.name_en: Dedicated Fund on Branding, Upgrading and Domestic Sales (BUD Fund)
programmes.funder: Trade and Industry Department, Government of the HKSAR
programmes.amount_note: Cumulative funding ceiling of HK$7 million per enterprise across the Mainland Programme and the Free Trade Agreement and Investment Agreement Programme, funding up to 50% of approved project cost on a matching basis, with a per-project cap (historically HK$1 million).
programmes.deadline_note: Applications are accepted all year round through the BUD Fund online system, with assessments made in batches.

procedure_steps.detail: Confirm the target market falls under the Mainland Programme or an applicable free trade agreement economy.
Prepare the project proposal covering branding, upgrading or domestic sales activities.
Submit through the BUD Fund online system with quotations and financial documents.
Vetting committee assessment.
Funding agreement and reimbursement of the government share against actual expenditure.

documents_required.doc: Business Registration Certificate and Certificate of Incorporation
Quotations from at least the required number of suppliers
Evidence of substantive business operations in Hong Kong

eligibility.other_note: Non-listed enterprises registered in Hong Kong under the Business Registration Ordinance with substantive business operations in Hong Kong at the time of application. Manufacturing and non-manufacturing SMEs both qualify.

programmes.source_snippet: The BUD Fund provides funding support to Hong Kong enterprises to develop brands, upgrade and restructure their operations and promote sales in the Mainland and FTA economies.

programmes.funder: Hong Kong Cyberport Management Company Limited
programmes.amount_note: Seed grant of HK$100,000 over a six-month period to develop a proof of concept for a digital technology idea, plus entrepreneurship training and mentorship. Successful graduates can progress to the Cyberport Incubation Programme.
programmes.deadline_note: Two intakes per year, historically with application windows around the first quarter and the third quarter.
programmes.reopen_note: CCMF has run two intakes per year for many years. Registration for the next intake opens on the Cyberport website; sign up for Cyberport notifications as the windows are typically only three to four weeks long.

procedure_steps.detail: Register and submit the application online during an open intake.
Preliminary screening of the idea and team.
Pitch to the assessment panel.
If successful, incorporate a Hong Kong company (if not already) and sign the funding agreement.
Deliver the six-month proof-of-concept project with milestone reporting.

documents_required.doc: Project budget and six-month milestone plan
Certificate of Incorporation and Business Registration Certificate once incorporated

eligibility.other_note: Open to Hong Kong residents and to companies incorporated in Hong Kong for not more than three years, with a digital technology idea at the concept or early prototype stage. Applicants may apply as individuals or teams and incorporate after selection.

programmes.source_snippet: The Cyberport Creative Micro Fund provides seed funding of HK$100,000 to support the realisation of digital tech ideas.

programmes.funder: Hong Kong Cyberport Management Company Limited
programmes.amount_note: Financial assistance of up to HK$500,000 over a 24-month incubation period, plus subsidised office space at Cyberport, mentorship, technical resources and access to investor networks.
programmes.deadline_note: Two intakes per year, with application windows announced on the Cyberport website.
programmes.reopen_note: The programme has run two intakes per year for many years and continues to do so. Monitor the Cyberport website and sign up for alerts; windows are typically four to six weeks.

procedure_steps.detail: Submit the online application with business plan and financial projections during an open intake.
Preliminary vetting.
Pitch to the admission panel.
If admitted, sign the incubation agreement and move into Cyberport (or take up the off-site option).
Draw down financial assistance against milestones over 24 months.

documents_required.doc: Certificate of Incorporation and Business Registration Certificate

eligibility.other_note: Digital technology startups incorporated in Hong Kong, normally for not more than five years, with the majority of the team based in Hong Kong. Non-local founders may apply but must incorporate and operate in Hong Kong.

programmes.source_snippet: The Cyberport Incubation Programme provides financial assistance of up to HK$500,000 and a range of support services to digital tech start-ups.

programmes.funder: Hong Kong Cyberport Management Company Limited
programmes.amount_note: Co-investment fund investing in Cyberport community startups typically at seed to Series A stage, on a matching basis alongside qualified lead investors. Individual investments are commonly in the range of a few million Hong Kong dollars.
programmes.deadline_note: Rolling. Applications are considered when a qualified lead investor has committed to the round.

procedure_steps.detail: Secure a term sheet from a qualified lead investor.
Submit the co-investment application to the Cyberport Macro Fund team.
Due diligence and investment committee review.
Co-investment on the lead investor's terms.

documents_required.doc: Certificate of Incorporation and Business Registration Certificate

eligibility.other_note: Hong Kong-incorporated digital technology startups, with priority to companies in the Cyberport community (incubatees, alumni and tenants). A qualified lead investor is required.

programmes.source_snippet: The Cyberport Macro Fund co-invests with private investors in Cyberport digital technology start-ups.

programmes.name_local: 科技園公司 創業培育計劃 - Ideation Programme
programmes.funder: Hong Kong Science and Technology Parks Corporation (HKSTP)
programmes.amount_note: Up to HK$100,000 in seed funding over a 12-month programme, plus co-working space at HKSTP, entrepreneurship training, mentorship and access to laboratories.
programmes.deadline_note: Applications are accepted with periodic assessment cut-offs (historically quarterly).
programmes.reopen_note: HKSTP runs recurring assessment cycles for Ideation. If a cut-off has just passed, the next is normally within three months.

procedure_steps.detail: Submit the online application with the technology idea and team profile.
Screening and interview.
Pitch to the assessment panel.
Admission to the 12-month programme, funding drawn against milestones.

documents_required.doc: Company incorporation documents if already incorporated

eligibility.other_note: Aspiring entrepreneurs and very early-stage technology teams. Company incorporation in Hong Kong is required during the programme rather than at application.

programmes.source_snippet: The Ideation Programme provides up to HK$100,000 and a 12-month support package to aspiring tech entrepreneurs.

programmes.name_local: 科技園公司 培育計劃（Incu-Tech / Incu-Bio / Incu-App）
programmes.funder: Hong Kong Science and Technology Parks Corporation (HKSTP)
programmes.amount_note: Financial support of up to approximately HK$1.29 million over three years for Incu-App and Incu-Tech style programmes and up to around HK$6 million over four years for Incu-Bio, covering rent subsidies, professional services, marketing and R&D, plus laboratory and cleanroom access at Science Park.
programmes.deadline_note: Applications accepted year round with periodic assessment cut-offs.
programmes.reopen_note: HKSTP runs recurring assessment cycles. If an intake cut-off is missed, the next one normally follows within a few months.

procedure_steps.detail: Choose the appropriate programme stream (Incu-Tech for general technology, Incu-Bio for biotechnology, Incu-App for smart applications).
Submit the online application with business plan and technology description.
Screening, due diligence and panel interview.
Admission and licence agreement for space at Science Park.
Draw down support against milestones over the programme term.

documents_required.doc: Certificate of Incorporation and Business Registration Certificate

eligibility.other_note: Technology startups incorporated in Hong Kong, normally within five years, undertaking R&D-based product development. Non-local founders are eligible if the company operates from Hong Kong.

programmes.source_snippet: HKSTP incubation programmes provide financial support, infrastructure and business services to technology start-ups.

programmes.name_local: 創新及科技基金 企業支援計劃（ESS）
programmes.name_en: Innovation and Technology Fund — Enterprise Support Scheme (ESS)
programmes.funder: Innovation and Technology Commission (ITC), Government of the HKSAR
programmes.amount_note: Funding on a matching basis of up to HK$10 million per project, covering up to 50% of total project cost, for in-house R&D by Hong Kong companies. The company owns the resulting IP. Project duration is normally up to 24 months.
programmes.deadline_note: Applications are accepted all year round through the ITF electronic submission system, with assessment by vetting panels held periodically.

procedure_steps.detail: Prepare the R&D project proposal with technical objectives, deliverables and budget.
Submit through the ITF online system with company and financial information.
Preliminary screening and, where required, a presentation to the vetting committee.
Approval and signing of the project agreement.
Milestone reporting and reimbursement of the government share of actual expenditure.

documents_required.doc: Project proposal with technical detail and deliverables
Audited financial statements for the past two years
Evidence of the company's matching funds

eligibility.other_note: Companies registered in Hong Kong under the Companies Ordinance with substantive business operations in Hong Kong. The project must be conducted mainly in Hong Kong and must not be a routine upgrade. Shell companies and companies without a track record of operations are not eligible.

programmes.source_snippet: The Enterprise Support Scheme provides funding support to private companies for their in-house R&D on a matching basis.

programmes.name_local: 大學科技初創企業資助計劃（TSSSU）
programmes.name_en: Technology Start-up Support Scheme for Universities (TSSSU)
programmes.funder: Innovation and Technology Commission (ITC), Government of the HKSAR
programmes.amount_note: Up to HK$1.5 million per startup per year for a maximum of three years, provided through the startup's host university. Each participating university receives an annual allocation and runs its own internal selection.
programmes.deadline_note: Each of the participating universities (HKU, CUHK, HKUST, PolyU, CityU, HKBU, LingnanU, EdUHK and others as designated) runs an annual internal call, typically with deadlines in the first half of the calendar year.
programmes.reopen_note: TSSSU runs annually with allocations to each participating university. Contact the knowledge transfer or entrepreneurship office of the relevant university for the next internal call date, since deadlines differ between institutions.

procedure_steps.detail: Confirm the startup has the required connection to a participating university (founded by current students, staff or recent graduates, or using university technology).
Apply through the university's knowledge transfer or entrepreneurship office during its internal call.
University selection panel assessment.
Award and funding agreement with the university.
Progress reporting to the university, which reports to ITC.

documents_required.doc: Evidence of the university connection (student or staff status, or technology licence)
Certificate of Incorporation and Business Registration Certificate

eligibility.other_note: Technology startups formed by current students, staff or graduates (usually within the past few years) of a participating Hong Kong university, or commercialising that university's research. Detailed criteria are set by each university.

programmes.source_snippet: TSSSU provides funding to universities to support their technology start-ups.

programmes.funder: Innovation and Technology Commission (ITC), Government of the HKSAR
programmes.amount_note: A HK$2 billion government co-investment fund that invests alongside selected co-investment partners (venture capital funds) into local innovation and technology startups, generally on a matching basis of roughly 1 government dollar to 2 private dollars. Startups do not apply directly.
programmes.deadline_note: No public application round for startups. Investment flows through appointed co-investment partners; startups raise from those partners.

procedure_steps.detail: Identify the ITVF co-investment partners listed on the ITF website.
Pitch to a co-investment partner and secure a lead investment.
The partner brings the ITVF in as a co-investor.
Standard investment documentation.

documents_required.doc: Certificate of Incorporation and Business Registration Certificate

eligibility.other_note: Local innovation and technology startups. Investment decisions are made by the co-investment partner; ITVF follows on matched terms.

programmes.source_snippet: The Innovation and Technology Venture Fund co-invests with venture capital funds in local innovation and technology start-ups.

programmes.funder: Innovation and Technology Commission (ITC), Government of the HKSAR
programmes.amount_note: Matching funding on a 1 (government) to 2 (company) basis of up to HK$200 million per project to set up new smart production lines in Hong Kong. The company must contribute at least two-thirds of the project cost.
programmes.deadline_note: Applications are accepted on a rolling basis with periodic assessment by the vetting committee.

procedure_steps.detail: Plan the smart production line, including equipment, automation and the Hong Kong production site.
Submit the application through the NIFS online system with the business case and financials.
Assessment covering technology content, economic benefit and financial capability.
Approval, funding agreement and milestone-based disbursement.
Operate the production line in Hong Kong for the required period after completion.

documents_required.doc: Project proposal covering the production line design and technology
Certificate of Incorporation and Business Registration Certificate
Audited financial statements for the past three years
Evidence of the company's matching contribution
Site or lease documentation for the Hong Kong production facility

eligibility.other_note: Companies registered in Hong Kong under the Companies Ordinance, setting up new smart production lines physically located in Hong Kong. Applicants must demonstrate the financial capability to fund at least two-thirds of the project cost.

programmes.source_snippet: The New Industrialisation Funding Scheme supports manufacturers in setting up new smart production lines in Hong Kong on a matching basis.
